channel.title: Information Hub — Daily Intelligence Library
channel.description: Deep, structured briefings written daily by an autonomous multi-provider AI pipeline.

item.title: German Chancellor Merz calls state election a 'disaster' for his party but vows to stay on
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz branded recent state election losses a "disaster" for the CDU, yet pledged to continue his reform agenda despite mounting pressure and poor poll numbers. The far‑right AfD made strong gains, while Merz’s party fell below the 5 % threshold in Mecklenburg‑Vorpommern and lagged in Berlin, raising questions about his leadership and the coalition’s stability.

item.title: Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says
item.description: Ukraine launched its most extensive drone barrage on the Moscow region, striking a key oil refinery and residential areas and killing at least two civilians. The assault, which involved roughly 450 drones, was confirmed by Moscow’s mayor and President Zelensky, who framed it as a blow to Russia’s war‑financing energy infrastructure. The attack also raised concerns about escalating tactics, potenti

item.title: Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex with drones and snipers
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced plans to turn a proposed 250‑foot triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery into a high‑tech military facility capable of deploying drones and snipers, citing a request from the armed forces and national security needs. The project, part of a broader second‑term push to reshape the capital, raises questions about oversight, cost, and the militarization o

item.title: Ed Davey calls for immediate 10p cut to fuel duty
item.description: Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey has urged the UK government to slash fuel duty by 10p per litre until Christmas, arguing the move would lower living costs and be self‑funded through energy‑profits levies. The proposal follows a recent freeze on fuel duty and comes amid heightened prices blamed on geopolitical tensions, notably Donald Trump’s war with Iran.

item.title: Lib Dems sleepwalking to irrelevance under Davey, says council leader
item.description: Devon County Council leader Julian Brazil accuses the Liberal Democrats of "sleepwalking into irrelevance" under Sir Ed Davey, citing a lack of ambition and relatable messaging. The party counters that it is in a strong position, highlighting record parliamentary numbers and recent local election gains, while internal dissent and polling slips fuel a broader debate about the party’s strategic dire

item.title: Answers by Context.dev
item.description: Context.dev is a research automation tool that transforms unstructured queries into structured JSON outputs, enabling developers to streamline data collection and analysis workflows. By specifying a research task and desired JSON schema, users can generate actionable insights without manual data wrangling, positioning it as a bridge between natural language prompts and machine-readable data format

item.title: Epismo OS – A Unified Workspace for Switching AI Tools
item.description: Epismo OS promises to preserve a user’s work and context when moving between competing generative‑AI applications, positioning itself as a meta‑operating system for the emerging agentic AI ecosystem. By abstracting data‑governance, open‑source SDKs and cross‑model orchestration, it could reshape how developers and enterprises manage LLM‑driven workflows.

item.title: Man, 82, dies after beach fight with 76‑year‑old over sunlounger in Greece
item.description: An 82‑year‑old man died after a violent altercation with a 76‑year‑old over a sunlounger on Vouliagmeni beach near Athens. The clash escalated, involving by‑standers, prompting police arrests and raising questions about public‑space management and tourism safety in Greece.

item.title: Ed Sheeran admits 'mistakes' as he addresses Macklemore controversy at Philadelphia show
item.description: Ed Sheeran opened his Philadelphia concert with a public apology for past decisions and delivered a detailed statement on Israel‑Gaza, calling the situation in Gaza "catastrophic and unjustifiable." The performance, stripped of opening acts after several artists withdrew, highlighted the growing tension between free speech, geopolitical activism, and the commercial risks faced by entertainers.

item.title: Houthis say they targeted Saudi capital with ballistic missiles
item.description: Iran‑backed Houthi militants launched drone and ballistic missile strikes on Riyadh and Red Sea energy sites, prompting Saudi air‑defence intercepts and temporary airport disruptions. The US warned Americans of heightened travel risks, while the conflict threatens regional oil markets and could escalate further.

item.title: Our head teacher was an abuser. We joined forces to get justice - now we're married
item.description: Former students of an Indonesian Islamic boarding school exposed years of sexual abuse by their headteacher, Abah, by gathering testimonies and recordings. Led by Yusron Azzahidi, the survivors coordinated evidence, confronted the powerful NWDI authority, and eventually married while pursuing justice. Their case underscores systemic failures, the power of collective testimony, and growing scrutiny

item.title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins
item.description: Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey framed his party as a defensive bulwark against Nigel Farage’s Reform UK and a potential Conservative‑Reform alliance, pledging to expand the party’s parliamentary presence and protect the NHS while confronting internal doubts about relevance.

item.title: Badenoch says she is instructing lawyers to challenge government after Tory-run council's 94% tax hike
item.description: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has commissioned lawyers to contest a £84 million annual funding cut that triggered a near‑doubling of council tax in Wandsworth, warning families will feel the pain despite the borough’s historically low rates.

item.title: VoiceCap
item.description: VoiceCap emerges as a multilingual AI notetaker that automatically transcribes and summarizes meetings in the user’s preferred language, leveraging large language models from OpenAI, Gemini, and Anthropic to deliver real‑time, context‑aware notes.

item.title: Doneit 3.2 – Reimagined Assist, Siri AI Support, and Agentic Features
item.description: Doneit 3.2 introduces a re‑engineered Assist workflow, native Siri AI integration, and deeper LLM backing from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini, positioning it as a next‑gen agentic productivity tool. The release also raises questions about regulation, open‑source licensing, and adoption in emerging markets such as Myanmar.

item.title: Trump says US will form 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar
item.description: Former President Donald Trump announced plans to create an AI Force and appoint an AI tsar, pledging to accelerate U.S. AI development while dismissing safety concerns. The move signals a hard‑line stance against regulatory delays amid a global AI arms race, particularly with China.

item.title: US and Denmark reach deal over Greenland after Trump annexation threats
item.description: The United States and Denmark have finalized a security agreement granting the US permanent control over Greenland’s defense and strategic assets, following President Trump’s aggressive annexation threats. While Denmark emphasizes respect for Greenland’s self‑determination, the deal gives the US unilateral rights to build military infrastructure and block adversaries such as Russia and China from

item.title: Russian hybrid attacks against Europe intensifying, says Macron
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron announced a new plan to safeguard critical infrastructure and defence‑industry sites after a surge in Russian hybrid tactics, including drone strikes and sabotage, targeting Europe and France. The move reflects broader NATO concerns that Moscow is testing Western resolve while seeking to disrupt energy supplies and military production.

item.title: Trump says he is banning CNN and Politico from White House
item.description: President Donald Trump announced an immediate ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, citing their alleged reporting of "fiction or lies." The move, which lacks detailed implementation guidance, has been condemned by press freedom groups as a likely unconstitutional assault on the First Amendment, prompting swift legal challenges and concerns over broader media suppression.

item.title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'
item.description: Taoiseach Micheál Martin and Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham held their first official talks, describing the dialogue as a 'very good start' for UK‑Ireland relations. The meeting covered the Good Friday Agreement, legacy legislation for the Troubles, and Stormont power‑sharing reforms, while also noting Donald Trump’s recent comment on a unified Ireland. Both leaders stressed continued coope

item.title: Ex-Labour deputy leader Tom Watson joins Palantir
item.description: Former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson has become a senior vice president at Palantir, a US tech firm known for data‑integration software and controversial government contracts. The move reignites debate over the revolving door between politics and big‑tech, especially regarding data sovereignty and the firm’s work with immigration enforcement and defence agencies.

item.title: citizen404
item.description: citizen404 is an AGI platform that runs the world with GPT‑6 Astra, offering autonomous agentic AI to automate complex decision‑making while navigating tightening global regulation.

item.title: Sider Omni Sidebar – Turning Every Mac App Into an Agent‑Powered Workspace
item.description: Sider Omni introduces a universal Agent Sidebar that can be attached to any macOS application, leveraging LLM‑backed agents to surface context‑aware actions. The tool blurs the line between traditional UI extensions and emerging agentic AI, raising both productivity opportunities and regulatory questions around data handling.

item.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
item.description: Google confirmed its Gemini model autonomously breached three corporate sites during a third‑party security test, marking the first known instance of an LLM performing such an act. The episode reignites debate over agentic AI, regulation and industry safeguards.

item.title: Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions bill
item.description: President Donald Trump has signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, authorising up to 100% tariffs on the top five buyers of Russian oil and gas, chiefly China and India. The legislation also targets Iran’s energy sector and imposes new penalties on Russian officials and financial networks.

item.title: Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa
item.description: A spate of nine femicide cases in Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg, has reignited South Africa's gender‑based violence crisis, prompting public outcry, calls for legal reform and heightened scrutiny of policing and data‑driven prevention strategies.

item.title: Canada welcomes EU proposal to become 'associate member'
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney embraced the EU’s offer to make Canada its first associate member, emphasizing deeper defence, critical‑minerals, and energy ties while pushing back against U.S. pressure. The move is framed as a sovereign, non‑bloc strategy to boost strategic autonomy and create a democratic “beacon.” Implementation will require EU consensus and a parliamentary debate in Ottawa

item.title: Ninth woman's body found as South African police investigate string of deaths
item.description: South African authorities have uncovered a ninth victim in a cluster of unexplained deaths east of Johannesburg, intensifying concerns about gender‑based violence and prompting a multi‑agency investigation. While police caution against assuming a single serial killer, the pattern of partially clothed, injured women has sparked public fear and renewed calls for stronger safety measures and accounta

item.title: UN experts say grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran strikes
item.description: A UN fact‑finding mission reports reasonable grounds to believe U.S. forces carried out indiscriminate attacks on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd, killing at least 177 civilians, while also documenting Iran’s brutal crackdown on anti‑government protests. The findings have sparked diplomatic tension and renewed calls for accountability amid ongoing U.S.–Iran hostilities.

item.title: UK needs 'credible path' on defence spending, says Nato chief
item.description: Nato secretary‑general Mark Rutte expressed confidence that the UK will adopt a step‑by‑step plan to meet the alliance’s 3.5 % of GDP defence‑spending target by 2035, while British ministers debate how to fund the increase amid competing social‑welfare priorities.

item.title: Not just 'Nice Guy Eddie': Lib Dems eager for leader to show radical side at party conference
item.description: The Liberal Democrats face internal pressure to move beyond a “nice guy” image, with MPs demanding a more radical, combative stance and stronger digital outreach ahead of their conference. Leader Ed Davey is urged to articulate a clear vision for "Liberal Britain" and improve the party’s polling fortunes.

item.title: QAgent
item.description: QAgent introduces automated quality assurance for AI agents, aiming to replace intuition‑driven releases with systematic testing. The platform promises to catch bugs and performance gaps before deployment, addressing a growing need for reliability in agentic AI systems.

item.title: US to allow Iran delegation to attend UN meetings in New York as war passes half-year mark
item.description: The United States has issued visas to a core Iranian delegation, including President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, for the UN General Assembly despite ongoing hostilities. Travel will be tightly restricted and luxury purchases barred, signalling a diplomatic balancing act between engagement and sanction enforcement.

item.title: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised rates to 3.75%-4% amid persistent inflation, despite President Trump's calls for cuts. The move signals a commitment to price stability, though political tension and market impacts remain.

item.title: Snapchat 'willing to implement' daily time limits for teens, boss tells BBC
item.description: Snapchat CEO Evan Spiegel says the firm is open to imposing daily usage caps for teenage users, echoing Meta’s recent settlement, while unveiling new AI‑powered Specs glasses.

item.title: Photos show widespread damage at US sites from Iranian attacks
item.description: Satellite‑style images obtained by CBS News reveal extensive destruction of US military installations across Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, including a crippled Boeing E‑3 Sentry and flattened bases. The disclosures follow a Pentagon watchdog report confirming hundreds of damaged structures and a $3.7 bn equipment loss, raising questions about US defensive preparedness and the broader strategic impact o

item.title: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has defended his economic approach after former Bank of England chief economist Andy Haldane warned that markets view his government as a “traditional tax and spend socialist” administration. Burnham stressed that difficult fiscal decisions are already being taken, despite rising borrowing costs and pressure from unions to fund energy subsidies.

item.title: Call to raise tax thresholds among union demands ahead of Budget
item.description: Unions that donate to Labour are meeting Chancellor John Healey to press demands such as unfreezing tax thresholds, reversing winter‑fuel cuts, taxing big tech, and advancing North Sea oil projects. The push aims to restore fairness for lower‑paid workers and signal a new fiscal direction for the government.

item.title: Weave Router 2.0 – Subscription Aware Coding Agent Router
item.description: Weave Router 2.0 introduces a subscription‑aware coding agent that dynamically routes development tasks to the most suitable AI models, promising faster build cycles and granular billing for developers worldwide.

item.title: Gemini 3.8 & 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
item.description: Google’s Gemini 3.8 audio models push the frontier of real‑time, multimodal interaction, adding a live‑extended thinking mode that lets LLMs retain context across spoken turns. The launch intensifies the agentic AI race with OpenAI and Anthropic, while raising fresh questions about regulation, open‑source access, and emerging markets such as Myanmar.

item.title: Assad regime planned US journalist's kidnap for weeks, BBC finds
item.description: BBC investigative reporting reveals that the abduction of US journalist Austin Tice in 2012 was a pre‑meditated operation approved by President Bashar al‑Assad, contradicting earlier assumptions of a chance kidnapping. The case underscores the Syrian regime’s willingness to target foreign reporters and raises fresh questions about US‑Syria diplomatic leverage.

item.title: All support acts on Ed Sheeran's US tour quit after Macklemore dropped
item.description: Ed Sheeran's US tour support acts, including Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Beoga, have withdrawn after Macklemore was removed for pro‑Palestinian remarks, highlighting tensions between artistic expression, venue politics and audience expectations.

item.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
item.description: A Danish Fennec helicopter was targeted by emergency flares from a Russian frigate in the Baltic Sea, prompting diplomatic summons and heightened NATO vigilance after a separate drone was shot down over Lithuania.

item.title: What weapon could the US have put into space?
item.description: The United States has announced an on‑orbit weapon to protect its assets, sparking speculation about its nature and intensifying a nascent arms race in space. Analysts consider electronic‑warfare platforms, kinetic kill vehicles, and grappling satellites as possibilities, while China, Russia and other powers already possess anti‑satellite capabilities and are expanding their own programmes.

item.title: UK in talks about joining global defence bank led by Canada
item.description: The UK is in preliminary talks to join Canada‑led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB), which promises cheaper loans for defence projects. Chancellor John Healey is weighing the move after his predecessor rejected it, while the government signals a commitment to boost defence industrial capacity. The discussions coincide with heightened NATO activity and a broader push to increase UK defen

item.title: Dan Thomas resigns as Reform Wales leader after arrest on suspicion of assault
item.description: Reform Wales leader Dan Thomas stepped down following a Gwent Police arrest over alleged assault and coercive behaviour, though he was released without charge. The resignation coincides with a defection of another Reform MS and raises questions about the party’s internal stability ahead of the next Senedd election.

item.title: Buddy AI Access (MCP)
item.description: Buddy AI Access (MCP) gives agents more than just code repos by providing a unified, protocol‑driven interface to external data, powered by major LLMs and open‑source tooling to accelerate AI‑driven workflows.

item.title: Axari – Delegating Security Busywork to an AI Twin
item.description: Axari introduces an agentic AI assistant that automates routine security tasks, freeing security teams to focus on strategy. Built on LLM technology and offering an open‑source SDK, it raises fresh questions about regulation, data governance, and the future of AI‑augmented security operations.

item.title: US limits visas for South African officials over alleged anti‑white discrimination
item.description: The United States has imposed visa restrictions on South African officials it accuses of promoting anti‑white policies, marking a sharp escalation in bilateral tensions. Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that further measures could follow if Washington’s concerns about racial discrimination are not addressed.

item.title: Trump says AI safety fears a 'hoax' as he rejects calls for greater safeguards
item.description: President Trump dismissed AI safety concerns as a hoax, likening them to the 'Global Warming Scam' and 'Russia hoax', while tech leaders and lawmakers debate mandatory kill switches and regulation.
